hook.text: A project has thousands of tasks — but only one sequence determines when it finishes.

buildup.text: CPM maps every task, its duration, and its dependencies — which tasks must finish before others start.

discovery.text: The longest chain of dependent tasks is the critical path — delay any one and the project is late.

twist.text: Non-critical tasks have float — they can slip without affecting the finish date.

climax.text: CPM was invented for the Polaris missile program — scheduling 3,000 contractors simultaneously.

punchline.text: Find the longest path and shorten it. That's how you finish a project faster.

quiz.question: What defines the critical path in a construction schedule?
options: The tasks that cost the most money to complete
The longest chain of dependent tasks that determines the project's minimum duration
The tasks assigned to the most experienced workers
